standard_prerequisites.name: The diagonal of a separated etale morphism is an open and closed immersion
standard_prerequisites.source_reference: Morphisms of Spaces, labels spaces-morphisms-lemma-etale-unramified and spaces-morphisms-lemma-diagonal-unramified-morphism (invoked at proof lines 1088 and 1090)
standard_prerequisites.use: They show that the complement $W_p$ of the diagonals in the $(p+1)$-fold fibre product is an open and closed subspace, so that the sections over it split off.

standard_prerequisites.name: The tensor power of the extension by zero splits along the complement of the diagonals
standard_prerequisites.source_reference: Same chapter spaces-cohomology.tex, label lemma-product-is-tensor-product (invoked at proof line 1095)
standard_prerequisites.use: It gives $(f_!\underline{\mathbf{Z}})^{\otimes p+1} = (W_p \to X)_!\underline{\mathbf{Z}} \oplus Rest$, which produces the comparison map towards the alternating power.

standard_prerequisites.name: The stalk computation identifying the quotient with the exterior power
standard_prerequisites.source_reference: Stalk computation over geometric points of $X$ (proof lines 1103-1114)
standard_prerequisites.use: It identifies the kernel of the map to $(W_p \to X)_!\underline{\mathbf{Z}}$ with the tensors carrying a repeated factor, which is exactly the kernel of the map to the alternating power.

core_obligations: Use that the diagonal is a closed immersion (separatedness) and an open immersion (etaleness) to see that $W_p$ is an open and closed subspace of $U^{p+1}$, and note that the action of $S_{p+1}$ on $W_p$ is free because the fixed points have been removed (proof lines 1085-1093).

Apply the tensor decomposition to write $(f_!\underline{\mathbf{Z}})^{\otimes p+1} = (W_p \to X)_!\underline{\mathbf{Z}} \oplus Rest$, and use the stalk computation to identify the kernel of the resulting map as generated by the tensors with a repeated factor, so that it factors through the alternating power (proof lines 1094-1128).
Conclude first that $\Hom(K^p, \mathcal{F})$ embeds functorially into $\Hom((W_p \to X)_!\underline{\mathbf{Z}}, \mathcal{F}) = \mathcal{F}(W_p)$ (proof lines 1129-1133).

Identify that subgroup with the anti-invariants: show that the surjection onto $K^p = \wedge^{p+1}f_!\underline{\mathbf{Z}}$ is the maximal anti-invariant quotient, i.e., that its kernel is generated by the local sections $s - \mathrm{sign}(\sigma)\sigma(s)$, which is checked on stalks (proof lines 1134-1142).
proof_roadmap: $W_p$ is open and closed, and the action is free (proof lines 1085-1093).
The decomposition of the tensor power and the comparison map (proof lines 1094-1128).
Embedding of $\Hom(K^p, \mathcal{F})$ into the sections over $W_p$ (proof lines 1129-1133).
difficulty_reason: The lemma computes the Hom group out of the alternating power of the extension by zero of the constant sheaf as the anti-invariant sections over the space of distinct ordered points (statement lines 1067-1082). The proof notes that the complement of the diagonals is open and closed with a free symmetric group action, decomposes the tensor power accordingly, identifies the kernel of the comparison map by a stalk computation, and finally shows that the map onto the alternating power is the maximal anti-invariant quotient. The stalk identification of the anti-invariants is the substance, so the claim is H2.
